{
  "findings": [

      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "The optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log datetimes",
      "body": "The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to a datetime.datetime value. Every nonempty optimized page therefore raises TypeError while building its cursors. value_from_cursor also leaves timestamp cursors numeric instead of converting them back to datetimes. This path needs DateTimePaginator's conversions, not the numeric paginator implementation."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/spans/buffer.py",
      "line": 197,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Changing Redis key types requires a migration or versioned keyspace",
      "body": "ZADD and ZSCAN now reuse the same span-buf:s:* keys that existing consumers populated as ordinary Redis sets. Buffered data survives deployment, and during a rolling rollout both implementations can access these keys. Redis rejects the incompatible operations with WRONGTYPE, preventing ingestion into existing segments and preventing their flush. Version the keyspace or provide a coordinated drain/migration and compatible read path before switching types."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py",
      "line": 71,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Handle requests without an organization member",
      "body": "The capability check dereferences organization_context.member for every non-superuser request, even when optimized_pagination was not requested. Organization-token authentication can authorize this endpoint without a user membership, leaving member as None; those requests now raise AttributeError instead of returning audit logs. Guard the optional membership and avoid evaluating this capability for requests using the normal paginator."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 882,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Django querysets do not support the advertised negative slicing",
      "body": "When advanced features are enabled, a negative cursor offset is passed directly to QuerySet slicing. Django explicitly rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'), so this branch cannot perform the advertised traversal. For example, Cursor(0, -1, False) fails immediately. Translate reverse traversal into nonnegative query bounds or reject the cursor with a pagination error."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 53,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Preserve timestamps when merging duplicate sorted-set members",
      "body": "ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. On replay, a payload already moved into its redirected segment can be ZADDed again under its original parent, leaving the same payload in both sets. The union then doubles its end timestamp, making an old replayed span appear far newer than other spans and causing ZPOPMIN to evict the wrong data. Use an aggregation mode that preserves the timestamp, such as MAX, for both unions."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 63,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Protect the segment span from eviction",
      "body": "Eviction considers only end timestamps and does not protect the root/segment span. With 1000 children and a root sharing their end timestamp, Redis's lexicographic tie-breaking can evict the root; children that outlive their parent create the same problem. This 1001-span segment was previously within the default limit, but now flush_segments can emit it without any is_segment span while has_root_span remains true. Preserve the root when selecting eviction victims."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/spans/buffer.py",
      "line": 449,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "The max_segment_spans setting is now silently ignored",
      "body": "Removing the span-count check leaves the existing max_segment_spans constructor argument unused, while insertion always applies a hard-coded limit of 1000. A buffer configured with max_segment_spans=100 can now emit up to 1000 spans, and one configured to allow larger segments silently loses data at 1000. Propagate the configured limit into insertion or retain appropriate enforcement instead of leaving a nonfunctional configuration argument."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 30,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "The reduced redirect limit can split valid deep segments",
      "body": "When ancestors arrive in separate batches, the redirect hash can contain a chain longer than 1000 entries. Evicting span payloads does not shorten that chain. The reduced loop bound silently stops before reaching the terminal segment, so a late child whose parent is more than 1001 redirects from the root is stored under an intermediate key and flushed as a separate segment. Retain the supported traversal depth or resolve/compress redirects rather than treating the payload limit as a redirect-depth limit."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: The optimized paginator cannot paginate audit-log datetimes
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil directly to a datetime.datetime value. Every nonempty optimized page therefore raises TypeError while building its cursors. value_from_cursor also leaves timestamp cursors numeric instead of converting them back to datetimes. This path needs DateTimePaginator's conversions, not the numeric paginator implementation.

findings.title: Changing Redis key types requires a migration or versioned keyspace
findings.body: ZADD and ZSCAN now reuse the same span-buf:s:* keys that existing consumers populated as ordinary Redis sets. Buffered data survives deployment, and during a rolling rollout both implementations can access these keys. Redis rejects the incompatible operations with WRONGTYPE, preventing ingestion into existing segments and preventing their flush. Version the keyspace or provide a coordinated drain/migration and compatible read path before switching types.

findings.title: Handle requests without an organization member
findings.body: The capability check dereferences organization_context.member for every non-superuser request, even when optimized_pagination was not requested. Organization-token authentication can authorize this endpoint without a user membership, leaving member as None; those requests now raise AttributeError instead of returning audit logs. Guard the optional membership and avoid evaluating this capability for requests using the normal paginator.

findings.title: Django querysets do not support the advertised negative slicing
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled, a negative cursor offset is passed directly to QuerySet slicing. Django explicitly rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'), so this branch cannot perform the advertised traversal. For example, Cursor(0, -1, False) fails immediately. Translate reverse traversal into nonnegative query bounds or reject the cursor with a pagination error.

findings.title: Preserve timestamps when merging duplicate sorted-set members
findings.body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. On replay, a payload already moved into its redirected segment can be ZADDed again under its original parent, leaving the same payload in both sets. The union then doubles its end timestamp, making an old replayed span appear far newer than other spans and causing ZPOPMIN to evict the wrong data. Use an aggregation mode that preserves the timestamp, such as MAX, for both unions.

findings.title: Protect the segment span from eviction
findings.body: Eviction considers only end timestamps and does not protect the root/segment span. With 1000 children and a root sharing their end timestamp, Redis's lexicographic tie-breaking can evict the root; children that outlive their parent create the same problem. This 1001-span segment was previously within the default limit, but now flush_segments can emit it without any is_segment span while has_root_span remains true. Preserve the root when selecting eviction victims.

findings.title: The max_segment_spans setting is now silently ignored
findings.body: Removing the span-count check leaves the existing max_segment_spans constructor argument unused, while insertion always applies a hard-coded limit of 1000. A buffer configured with max_segment_spans=100 can now emit up to 1000 spans, and one configured to allow larger segments silently loses data at 1000. Propagate the configured limit into insertion or retain appropriate enforcement instead of leaving a nonfunctional configuration argument.

findings.title: The reduced redirect limit can split valid deep segments
findings.body: When ancestors arrive in separate batches, the redirect hash can contain a chain longer than 1000 entries. Evicting span payloads does not shorten that chain. The reduced loop bound silently stops before reaching the terminal segment, so a late child whose parent is more than 1001 redirects from the root is stored under an intermediate key and flushed as a separate segment. Retain the supported traversal depth or resolve/compress redirects rather than treating the payload limit as a redirect-depth limit.
